items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bishop and Eddy de Hass, who later changed his namee for Eddie O'Hare, arrived in Paris about the same time as I.

ctx.x: Hans had his trio and his style was a little like Lester Young and Stan Getz. For a musical variety show, this set up was alright because there was the old style New Orleans music of Ken Colyer, the more modern Middle jazz style of me and my band, and the modern style of the 1950's played by Hans Kohler.

I closed at the Faun the 30th of September and arrived in Paris the 2nd of October. I had been in touch with the trombone player Bill Tamper, whom I had toured with a few days on another occasion, and I had signed Bill for my coming tour to replace Herman Wilson who had stayed in Germany with Donald Brown. Bishop and Eddy de Hass, who later changed his namee for Eddie O'Hare, arrived in Paris about the same time as I. We also had engaged a male singer this time to make the tour as there were no girl…

After seven good rehearsals, we had a very nice repertoire. We accompanied Tommy on three numbers and he did one at the piano which was "black coffee" and I liked this number better than any of the others he did. I don't remember what Tommy had been doing in Europe and I don't remember how I happened to get in touch with him, maybe through Bish. He had a big Cadillac car and a fine blonde Swedish chick.
